Episodes 1 to 5 of 18 are authored: 246 entities, 1,669 exact mentions in original-en and 1,665 in modern-en, 245 of the 246 bound in the older edition and 243 in the modern one, 50 focused tests passing, content revision 2026-09-14.5. NEXT: episode 6 (Hades, 402 paragraphs), the funeral -- the largest named cast so far, and where Simon Dedalus, Martin Cunningham, Jack Power, Ned Lambert, John Henry Menton, Joe Hynes and Rudolph Bloom all become people rather than names. 6,148 paragraphs remain; the long ones are 15 (Circe, 1,441), 17 (Ithaca, 654), 11 (Sirens, 635), 12 (566) and 10 (546); episode 18 (Penelope) is eight paragraphs of monologue and will be the densest in the book.

THE RULE THAT MATTERS MOST: A SURNAME IN THIS BOOK IS ALMOST NEVER ONE MAN, SO KEY BY DEFAULT AND ALIAS ONLY ON PROOF. The 'Bloom' table never defaults and 4:38 -- SLIEVE BLOOM, the mountains in Offaly -- is deliberately not a key in it; a test asserts both. Episode 5 added nine more keys of the same kind. THE SHARPEST ONE: 'Leopold' is Bloom at 5:67 and THE DUKE OF ALBANY at 5:121, twelve lines later, where Bloom notices that one of the old queen's sons had his own name. And 'Peter' is three people in six paragraphs -- Peter Claver, Peter Carey and the apostle -- with Bloom himself mixing up the first two out loud.

THE OCCURRENCE LIST HAS NOW REACHED BACK INTO SIGNED-OFF CHAPTERS TWICE: Columbanus at 2:73 (found while authoring episode 3) and MICHAEL'S HOST at 1:318 (found while authoring episode 5). Both are bound now and both are pinned by tests. Run it over every new name; it is the first and most productive check in this book.

THE MODERN EDITION IS A REWRITE AND CHANGES THE CAST OF A PARAGRAPH IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. It DELETES names (Chrysostomos 1:9, Mercury 1:293, Loyola 1:101, Adam Findlater and Dan Tallon 4:37, Hanlon 4:13) and it SUPPLIES names Joyce did not write (Aristotle 3:0, Brian Boru 3:57, Deasy 3:10, Queen Victoria 3:94, M'Coy 5:27). Two entities are therefore reachable in one edition only: BRIAN BORU in the modern edition alone, ADAM FINDLATER in the older alone, both recorded as omittedEntities for the other. It also respells freely: Ferrando/Fernando, Patk/Patrick, Raschid/Rashid, Occam/Ockham, Joachim Abbas/Joachim of Fiore, Columbanus/Saint Columban, Mairy/Mary, Mohammed/Muhammad, My missus/My wife. Check both editions before writing any card that turns on a name.

A SILENT BINDER LIMITATION THAT APPLIES TO EVERY BOOK IN THIS LIBRARY: reviewed_aliases.py guards alias matches with \w, AND AN UNDERSCORE SATISFIES \w, so an alias whose occurrence sits inside Gutenberg italics (_like this_) BINDS NOTHING AND NOTHING REPORTS IT. It has bitten twice here -- '_Los Demiurgos_' at 3:1 and '_Matcham's Masterstroke_' at 4:162 -- and both are keyed now. test_no_alias_in_this_package_is_hidden_by_italics is the standing check. Run over all 18 episodes it reports two more, both still ahead: STEPHEN at 15:1133 inside a stage direction, and PATRICE at 16:212, which is NOT Patrice Egan but 'the faubourg Saint Patrice called Ireland for short'.

BLOOM HAS A SECOND NAME AND IT HAS ITS OWN CARD: HENRY FLOWER, what he writes under and collects letters under at Westland row. The alias is safe for the whole book. Martha, his correspondent, is bound at 5:78 and 5:80 and becomes MARTHA OF BETHANY at 5:87, where the name slides out of the letter into a painting. Deliberately unbound and listed in the README: THE WOMAN OUTSIDE THE GROSVENOR, who occupies fifteen paragraphs and is never named or stably described; O'Connell STREET at 5:9; Cantrell and Cochrane's ginger ale at 5:65 and 5:101, which is a firm and not the schoolboy Cochrane of episode 2; and the shops of Dublin, which keep their owners' names and are not people. No edition byte was touched. This lane never sets appStatus.
